front: K for reversed or doubled equations?
back: Reverse: 1/K. Doubled coefficients: K².

K = [NH₃]² / ([N₂][H₂]³)

front: Effect of adding more reactant on equilibrium position and K?
back: Position shifts right to use up some added reactant; K unchanged (temperature constant).

front: Effect of increasing pressure on N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃?
back: Shifts right, towards fewer moles of gas (2 vs 4), so yield of NH₃ increases. No effect if gas moles are equal on both sides.

front: Effect of raising temperature on an exothermic equilibrium?
back: Shifts in the endothermic (backward) direction to absorb heat; yield falls and K decreases.
N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, ΔH < 0: ~200 atm, ~450 °C, Fe catalyst — a compromise between yield, rate and cost; NH₃ removed by cooling.

front: Contact process key equilibrium and conditions?
back: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃, ΔH < 0: ~450 °C, 1–2 atm, V₂O₅ catalyst; high conversion already at low pressure.

front: At equilibrium, are concentrations of reactants and products equal?
back: Not necessarily — they are constant. It is the forward and reverse rates that are equal.

front: Why must the system be closed for equilibrium?
back: No matter can enter or leave; otherwise a product (e.g. a gas) escapes and the reaction goes to completion.

front: Are pure solids and liquids included in K?
back: No — in heterogeneous equilibria their concentrations are constant and are left out (e.g. CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g): K = [CO₂]).
Reactant concentrations fall and product concentrations rise until both level off (horizontal lines) at equilibrium.

front: Units of K in IB Chemistry?
back: K is treated as unitless in IB (strictly it uses activities); do not include units.
Same expression as K but using concentrations at any moment, not necessarily at equilibrium.

front: (HL) Approximation when K is very small?
back: Assume x is negligible compared with initial concentrations ([A]₀ − x ≈ [A]₀) to avoid a quadratic; valid when K ≪ 1.

front: (HL) H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI: 1.0 mol each in 1.0 dm³, 0.80 mol HI at equilibrium. K?

back: ΔG⦵ = −RT ln K: ΔG⦵ < 0 ↔ K > 1; ΔG⦵ > 0 ↔ K < 1.
